questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning (IRACP) Directions, 2025 for commercial banks, an account is classified as NPA if its regular or ad hoc credit limits have not been reviewed or renewed within how many days from the due date or date of ad hoc sanction?

options.text: 180 days
90 days
60 days
365 days

solution.concept: NPA trigger for unreviewed credit limits
solution.explanation: Among the conditions for NPA classification, the IRACP Directions list an account where the regular or ad hoc credit limits have not been reviewed or renewed within 180 days from the due date or the date of ad hoc sanction.
steps: Count from due date / date of ad hoc sanction
solution.why_others_wrong: 90 days is the overdue norm for term loans; 60 days ends SMA-1; 365 days is not a period in this rule.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 180 days

fact_checks.claim: an account where the regular / ad hoc credit limits have not been reviewed / renewed within 180 days from the due date / date of ad hoc sanction

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, stock audit at annual intervals by external agencies is mandatory for NPAs with a balance of at least:

options.text: ₹1 crore
₹25 crore
₹5 crore
₹50 lakh

solution.explanation: To make stock valuation more reliable and reduce divergence, the Directions make annual stock audit by external agencies (appointed under Board-approved guidelines) mandatory for NPAs with a balance of ₹5 crore and above.
steps: Annual stock audit by external agency is mandatory
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1 crore, ₹25 crore and ₹50 lakh are not the threshold in the Directions.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹5 crore

fact_checks.claim: Stock audit at annual intervals by external agencies ... shall be mandatory in cases of NPAs with balance of ₹5 crore and above

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Over which of the following does the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) NOT have regulatory oversight?

options.text: Insolvency professional agencies
Asset reconstruction companies
Information utilities
Insolvency professionals

solution.explanation: IBBI describes itself as a unique regulator of both a profession and processes: it has regulatory oversight over insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, insolvency professional entities and information utilities. Asset reconstruction companies are registered and regulated by RBI under the SARFAESI Act.
steps: IBBI oversees IPs, IPAs, IPEs and IUs
solution.why_others_wrong: IPAs, information utilities and insolvency professionals are all under IBBI's oversight.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Asset reconstruction companies

fact_checks.claim: It has regulatory oversight over the Insolvency Professionals, Insolvency Professional Agencies, Insolvency Professional Entities and Information Utilities
ARCs are registered under Section 3 of the ... SARFAESI Act and regulated using the powers vested with the Reserve Bank thereunder

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, special mention account (SMA) categories differ for revolving facilities such as cash credit or overdraft. Which SMA sub-category is NOT defined for such revolving facilities?

options.text: SMA-1
SMA-2
None; all three apply equally to revolving facilities
SMA-0

solution.explanation: For loans other than revolving facilities, SMA-0 (up to 30 days overdue), SMA-1 (31-60 days) and SMA-2 (61-90 days) are defined. For cash credit/overdraft, the table has only SMA-1 and SMA-2, based on the outstanding remaining continuously above the sanctioned limit or drawing power (whichever is lower) for more than 30 up to 60 days and more than 60 up to 90 days.
steps: CC/OD: only SMA-1 (30-60 days) and SMA-2 (60-90 days)
solution.why_others_wrong: SMA-1 and SMA-2 do apply to revolving facilities, so they are not the answer, and the fourth option is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: SMA-0

fact_checks.claim: Loans in the nature of revolving facilities like cash credit/overdraft ... SMA-1 More than 30 days and up to 60 days; SMA-2 More than 60 days and up to 90 days (SMA-0 Up to 30 days listed only for loans other than revolving facilities)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank financed an industrial project with a moratorium on payment of interest during the gestation period. The project is still within the moratorium. Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, how is the unpaid interest treated?

options.text: It is overdue from the first quarter, so the account becomes NPA after 90 days
The account is classified as substandard but income may still be recognised
It becomes 'due' only after the moratorium is over, so the account does not become NPA on this ground
The account is classified as SMA-2 until the moratorium ends

solution.explanation: For finance to industrial projects or agricultural plantations with a moratorium on interest, interest becomes 'due' only after the moratorium or gestation period is over; such amounts do not become overdue, and hence the account does not become NPA, with reference to the date of debit of interest.
steps: Moratorium running → interest not yet due
Not overdue → no NPA on this ground
solution.why_others_wrong: Interest that is not due cannot be overdue, so neither NPA nor SMA classification arises; no substandard classification applies.
solution.final_answer: Option C: It becomes 'due' only after the moratorium is over, so the account does not become NPA on this ground

fact_checks.claim: where moratorium is available for payment of interest, payment of interest becomes 'due' only after the moratorium or gestation period is over. Such amounts of interest do not become overdue and hence do not become NPA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under a resolution plan implemented under RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, lenders sanction additional finance to the borrower. How may a bank classify this additional finance?

options.text: Always as NPA until the entire restructured debt is repaid
As a standard asset permanently, whatever the account's later performance
As a loss asset, since it is lent to a stressed borrower
As a standard asset during the monitoring period, if the account performs satisfactorily; otherwise in the same category as the restructured debt

solution.explanation: Additional finance approved under a resolution plan (including an IBC plan approved by the Adjudicating Authority) may be treated as standard during the monitoring period, provided the account shows satisfactory performance. If the restructured asset fails to perform or does not qualify for upgrade at the end of the monitoring period, the additional finance is placed in the same asset classification category as the restructured debt.
steps: During monitoring period + satisfactory performance → standard
Failure / no upgrade → same category as restructured debt
solution.why_others_wrong: It is neither automatically NPA nor permanently standard, and there is no rule making it a loss asset.
solution.final_answer: Option D: As a standard asset during the monitoring period, if the account performs satisfactorily; otherwise in the same category as the restructured debt

fact_checks.claim: Any additional finance approved under the resolution plan ... may be treated by a bank as standard asset during the monitoring period under the approved resolution plan, provided the account demonstrates satisfactory performance during the monitoring period

If the restructured asset fails to perform satisfactorily during the monitoring period or does not qualify for upgradation at the end of the monitoring period, the additional finance shall be placed in the same asset classification category as the restructured debt

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A borrower's cash credit account with a bank has been classified as NPA. The same bank had also discounted bills drawn under a letter of credit (LC) in the borrower's favour, which are not yet due. Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, how may the LC-backed bills be treated?

options.text: They may not be classified as NPA, unless the LC is not honoured on the due date and the borrower does not make good the amount immediately
They must be classified as NPA at once, since classification is borrower-wise
They become NPA only if the LC-issuing bank is itself classified as weak
They are written off along with the cash credit account

solution.concept: Exception for bills discounted under LC
solution.explanation: Although classification is normally borrower-wise, the Directions say bills discounted under an LC favouring a borrower may not be classified as NPA when another facility of the borrower is NPA. If the documents are not accepted or the LC-issuing bank does not pay on the due date and the borrower does not immediately make good the amount, the bills become NPA at once.
steps: Borrower-wise rule has an exception for LC-backed bills
Default under LC + no immediate payment → NPA
solution.why_others_wrong: The borrower-wise rule is expressly relaxed here; the issuing bank's health is not the test; no write-off is required.
solution.final_answer: Option A: They may not be classified as NPA, unless the LC is not honoured on the due date and the borrower does not make good the amount immediately

fact_checks.claim: The bills discounted under Letter of Credit (LC) favouring a borrower may not be classified as NPA, when any other facility granted to the borrower is classified as NPA

in case documents under LC are not accepted on presentation or the payment under the LC is not made on the due date ... and the borrower does not immediately make good the amount ... the outstanding bills discounted shall immediately be classified as NPA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An asset reconstruction company (ARC) registered under the SARFAESI Act does not have a net owned fund of ₹1,000 crore. According to RBI's FAQs on ARCs (September 2026), can it act as a resolution applicant under the IBC to acquire a financial asset (debt)?

options.text: No; only ARCs with NOF of at least ₹1,000 crore can be resolution applicants for any purpose
Yes; acquisition of debt is a permitted activity for ARCs, so the ₹1,000 crore NOF condition need not be met
No; ARCs can never be resolution applicants under the IBC
Yes, but only with prior approval of IBBI

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say that since acquisition of debt falls within 'securitisation' and 'asset reconstruction' under the SARFAESI Act, ARCs need not meet the conditions of paragraph 18 of the ARC Directions, 2025, including the ₹1,000 crore net owned fund, to act as resolution applicant for acquiring a financial asset.
steps: Acquisition of debt = permitted ARC activity
₹1,000 crore NOF condition does not apply to it
solution.why_others_wrong: The ₹1,000 crore NOF condition applies to other resolution-applicant roles, not to acquiring debt; IBBI approval is not the condition.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Yes; acquisition of debt is a permitted activity for ARCs, so the ₹1,000 crore NOF condition need not be met

fact_checks.claim: acquisition of debt is a permitted activity for ARCs. Therefore, ARCs need not meet the conditions specified in paragraph 18 of the ... (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions, 2025 ..., inter alia, a net owned fund of ₹1000 crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank has three borrowers with unhedged foreign currency exposure. Using the ratio of likely loss to EBID: X has a total exposure of ₹500 crore and a ratio of 40%; Y has ₹200 crore and 80%; Z has ₹300 crore and 12%. Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, what incremental provision (over the standard asset provision) must the bank hold on these three exposures together?

options.text: ₹3.6 crore
₹3.2 crore
₹4.2 crore
₹2.0 crore

solution.concept: Incremental provisioning for unhedged foreign currency exposure
solution.explanation: The table prescribes nil up to 15%, 20 bps for more than 15% up to 30%, 40 bps for more than 30% up to 50%, 60 bps for more than 50% up to 75% and 80 bps above 75%, on the total credit exposure. X: 40 bps × 500 = ₹2.0 crore; Y: 80 bps × 200 = ₹1.6 crore; Z: nil. Total ₹3.6 crore.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹3.2 crore applies 60 bps to Y (that slab ends at 75%); ₹4.2 crore wrongly adds 20 bps on Z; ₹2.0 crore counts X only.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹3.6 crore

fact_checks.claim: Up to 15 per cent 0; More than 15 per cent and up to 30 per cent 20 bps; More than 30 per cent and up to 50 per cent 40 bps; More than 50 per cent and up to 75 per cent 60 bps; More than 75 per cent 80 bps (incremental provisioning on the total credit exposures over and above extant standard asset provisioning)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank with total assets of ₹10,000 crore has these net funded country exposures: ₹200 crore to a country in ECGC category C1 (moderately high risk); ₹100 crore, all short-term (contractual maturity under 180 days), to a category B1 country (moderately low risk); and ₹50 crore to a category A2 country (low risk). It uses the lower provisioning allowed for short-term exposures. Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, what is its minimum country risk provision?

options.text: ₹55.00 crore
₹51.25 crore
₹51.375 crore
₹50.00 crore

solution.explanation: Country risk provisions apply only where the net funded exposure is 1% or more of total assets (here ₹100 crore), at 0.25% (A1/A2), 5% (B1), 20% (B2), 25% (C1) and 100% (C2/D); short-term exposures may carry 25% of the requirement. C1: 25% of 200 = ₹50 crore. B1: 5% of 100 = ₹5 crore, × 25% = ₹1.25 crore. A2: ₹50 crore is below 1% of assets, so nil. Total ₹51.25 crore.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹55 crore ignores the short-term relief; ₹51.375 crore wrongly provides 0.25% on the A2 exposure below the 1% threshold; ₹50 crore drops the B1 exposure, which meets the 'one per cent or more' test.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹51.25 crore

fact_checks.claim: Moderately Low Risk B1 5; Moderate Risk B2 20; Moderately High Risk C1 25; ... A bank shall make provision for country risk in respect of a country where its net funded exposure is one per cent or more of its total assets
A bank may make a lower level of provisioning (say 25 per cent of the requirement) in respect of short-term exposures (i.e. exposures with contractual maturity of less than 180 days)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A borrower hit by a natural calamity has outstanding debt of ₹40 crore with a bank, all in term loans. A resolution plan is implemented under Chapter VI-A of RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 and, later, a second restructuring under the same Chapter becomes necessary (assume the outstanding stays ₹40 crore). Under the IRACP Directions, 2025, what additional specific provision applies, and when can it be written back?

options.text: ₹2 crore (5% once); after the borrower pays at least ₹4 crore (10%)
₹4 crore (5% for each instance); after one year from implementation, whatever the repayment
₹8 crore (20%); only when the entire debt is repaid
₹4 crore (5% for each instance); after the borrower pays at least ₹8 crore (20%) without slipping into NPA and without another restructuring

solution.concept: Additional provisioning on resolution under Chapter VI-A
solution.explanation: A bank must make an additional specific provision of 5% of the outstanding debt when a plan is implemented under Chapter VI-A, and another 5% for each instance of repeated restructuring (over and above prudential provisions, capped at 100%). It may be written back once the borrower pays at least 20% of the outstanding debt without slipping into NPA and without another restructuring. The one-year write-back applies only when the debt is entirely non-fund-based or cash credit/overdraft type.
steps: Write-back: borrower pays ≥ 20% = ₹8 crore, no NPA, no fresh restructuring
solution.why_others_wrong: Repeated restructuring attracts 5% per instance, not once; 10% repayment is not the write-back test; the one-year route is only for non-fund-based or CC/OD debt; 20% is the repayment test, not the provision.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹4 crore (5% for each instance); after the borrower pays at least ₹8 crore (20%) without slipping into NPA and without another restructuring

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall make an additional specific provision of five percent of the outstanding debt ... For accounts where repeated restructuring is necessitated ... additional specific provisioning of five per cent of the outstanding debt for each instance of restructuring

may be written back upon the borrower paying at least 20% of the outstanding debt with the bank, without slipping into NPA post implementation of the restructuring, and without being subjected to another restructuring

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about asset reconstruction companies (ARCs), based on RBI's FAQs on ARCs (September 2026):
I. Yield on security receipts (SRs) is recognised only after full redemption of the entire principal amount of the SRs.
II. An ARC may distribute upside income on a priority basis to one class of SR holders over others.
III. Clauses such as 'NAV Protection Clauses' that delink the management fee from the ARC's performance are inconsistent with RBI's ARC Directions.
Which of the above are correct?

options.text: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III

solution.concept: Distribution of SR income and management fee
solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say yield on SRs is recognised only after full redemption of the entire principal of SRs and upside income only after full redemption of SRs; ARCs may not distribute yield or upside income on a priority basis to one class of SR holders. The management fee must be linked to performance and actual recoveries; NAV protection clauses that delink it are inconsistent with the Directions.
steps: I: correct (yield after full principal redemption)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing II is wrong, because priority distribution to one class is not permitted.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: yield on SRs shall be recognised only after the full redemption of the entire principal amount of SRs, and upside income shall be recognised only after the full redemption of SRs ... ARCs are not permitted to distribute yield or upside income on a priority basis to one class of SR holders

The management fee charged by ARCs must be linked to the performance of the ARC ... Any practice aimed at delinking the management fee from the performance of ARCs by clauses like 'NAV Protection Clauses' is inconsistent with the principles of the ... Directions, 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, overdrafts given to Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) account holders, within the limits and conditions set by the Department of Financial Services, are classified as lending to:

options.text: Agriculture
Social Infrastructure
Housing
Micro Enterprises

solution.explanation: The Directions list overdrafts to PMJDY account holders (as per DFS limits and conditions) among other loans eligible under the MSME category, to be categorised as lending to Micro Enterprises.
steps: PMJDY OD → MSME category → Micro Enterprises
solution.why_others_wrong: The Directions place it under Micro Enterprises, not agriculture, social infrastructure or housing.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Micro Enterprises

fact_checks.claim: Overdraft to Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) account holders as per limits and conditions prescribed by Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance from time to time, which shall be categorised as lending to Micro Enterprises

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank credit to NHB-approved Housing Finance Companies for on-lending for individual dwelling units qualifies as priority sector (Housing) under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025 subject to an aggregate loan limit per borrower of:

options.text: ₹10 lakh
₹35 lakh
₹20 lakh
₹50 lakh

solution.explanation: Bank credit to HFCs approved by NHB for refinance, for on-lending for purchase/construction/reconstruction of individual dwelling units or slum clearance and rehabilitation, is PSL under 'Housing' subject to an aggregate loan limit of ₹20 lakh per borrower.
steps: HFC on-lending for housing → ₹20 lakh per borrower
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹10 lakh is the agriculture term-lending limit for NBFC on-lending; ₹35 lakh and ₹50 lakh are not this limit.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹20 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Bank credit to Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), approved by NHB for their refinance, for on-lending for the purpose of purchase/construction/reconstruction of individual dwelling units ... subject to an aggregate loan limit of ₹20 lakh per borrower, under 'Housing' category

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the 'Others' category of RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, bank loans to Self Help Groups or Joint Liability Groups for purposes other than agriculture or MSME (such as social needs or house repair) qualify up to:

options.text: ₹1 lakh
₹2 lakh
₹10 lakh

solution.explanation: Loans not exceeding ₹2.00 lakh by banks to SHGs/JLGs for activities other than agriculture or MSME — for social needs, construction or repair of houses, construction of toilets or any viable common activity — qualify under 'Others'.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1 lakh is the limit for loans to distressed persons; ₹10 lakh and ₹50,000 are not limits for this item.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹2 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Loans not exceeding ₹2.00 lakh provided by banks to SHG/JLG for activities other than agriculture or MSME, viz., loans for meeting social needs, construction or repair of house, construction of toilets or any viable common activity started by SHGs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's PSL FAQs (September 2026), to which RBI department does a bank apply to get registered for trading Priority Sector Lending Certificates?

options.text: Financial Inclusion and Development Department, Central Office
Department of Payment and Settlement Systems
Department of Supervision
Foreign Exchange Department

solution.explanation: Banks request registration from RBI's Financial Inclusion and Development Department, Central Office, submitting their DEA Fund code, customer identification number and RBI current account number.
steps: Give DEA Fund code, CIN, RBI current account number
solution.why_others_wrong: PSL, and hence PSLC registration, is handled by FIDD, not the payments, supervision or forex departments.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Financial Inclusion and Development Department, Central Office

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank loans of up to ₹12 crore per borrower for building health care facilities qualify as priority sector under 'Social Infrastructure'. For commercial banks, in which centres must such facilities be located?

options.text: Tier II to Tier VI centres
Only Tier I centres
Tier IV to Tier VI centres only
Any centre, without restriction

solution.explanation: Social infrastructure covers loans up to ₹8 crore per borrower for schools, drinking water and sanitation facilities, and loans up to ₹12 crore per borrower for building health care facilities in Tier II to Tier VI centres.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tier I centres are excluded, so 'only Tier I' and 'any centre' are wrong; Tier IV–VI is too narrow.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Tier II to Tier VI centres

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to a limit of ₹12 crore per borrower for building health care facilities in Tier II to Tier VI centres
Loans up to a limit of ₹8 crore per borrower for setting up schools, drinking water facilities and sanitation facilities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A Small Finance Bank's ANBC on the relevant date is ₹20,000 crore, higher than its CEOBSE. Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, what are its overall PSL target, micro enterprises sub-target and weaker sections sub-target?

options.text: ₹8,000 crore; ₹1,500 crore; ₹2,400 crore
₹15,000 crore; ₹1,500 crore; ₹3,000 crore
₹12,000 crore; ₹1,500 crore; ₹2,400 crore
₹12,000 crore; ₹1,600 crore; ₹2,400 crore

solution.explanation: SFBs: total PSL 60%, micro enterprises 7.5%, weaker sections 12% of ANBC or CEOBSE, whichever is higher. 60% × 20,000 = 12,000; 7.5% × 20,000 = 1,500; 12% × 20,000 = 2,400 (₹ crore).
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹8,000 crore uses the 40% target of commercial banks; ₹15,000/₹3,000 crore use RRB rates (75%, 15%); ₹1,600 crore uses 8% for micro enterprises.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹12,000 crore; ₹1,500 crore; ₹2,400 crore

fact_checks.claim: Small Finance Banks: Total Priority Sector [60] per cent of ANBC ... or CEOBSE, whichever is higher; Micro Enterprises 7.5 per cent; Advances to Weaker Sections 12 percent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, in what language must each retail outlet or sub-agent of a Business Correspondent post the sign indicating its status as a service provider for the bank?

options.text: English only
Hindi and English only
Any language chosen by the BC
The local (vernacular) language

questions.question_text: According to the Government's note on 12 years of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (August 2026), which of the following is true of PM-JDY accounts?

options.text: Only individuals aged 18 to 60 can open one
A joint account can also be opened
A minimum balance of ₹500 must be maintained

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, which of the following is NOT treated as a 'Banking Outlet'?

options.text: An extension counter that meets the four-hours, five-days definition
A mobile branch
A fixed-point unit manned by a Business Correspondent that meets the definition
An ultra small branch that meets the definition

solution.concept: What counts as a Banking Outlet
solution.explanation: Extension counters, satellite offices, part-shifted branches, ultra small branches and specialised branches count as Banking Outlets (or part-time outlets) if they meet the definition. ATMs, e-lobbies, bunch note acceptor machines, cash deposit machines, e-kiosks and mobile branches are not Banking Outlets.
steps: Mobile branches, ATMs, CDMs, e-kiosks → not outlets
Extension counters, USBs, BC fixed points meeting the definition → outlets
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are expressly counted when they satisfy the definition.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A mobile branch

fact_checks.claim: ATMs, E- lobbies, Bunch Note Acceptor Machines (BNAM), Cash Deposit Machines (CDM), E- Kiosks and Mobile Branches will not be treated as 'Banking Outlets'

Extension Counters, Satellite Offices, Part-shifted Branches, Ultra Small Branches and Specialised Branches, subject to their satisfying the definition given above, shall be treated as independent 'Banking Outlets' or 'Part-time Banking Outlets'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank sets up a Central Processing Centre that processes loans, verifies documents and issues cheque books and demand drafts on requests from its outlets. Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, it is a:

options.text: Back Office, which is not permitted direct interface with customers
Banking Outlet, since it carries out banking functions
Part-time Banking Outlet
Digital Banking Unit

solution.explanation: A 'Back Office' is a CPC or office that exclusively handles functions such as data processing, loan processing, verification of documents and issue of cheque books and demand drafts on requests from other Banking Outlets. Direct interface with customers is not permitted.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: During a year a bank opens 120 full-time Banking Outlets, 26 of them in Unbanked Rural Centres (URCs). It also opens three part-time outlets in URCs, each working 5 hours a day on 4 days a week. Applying the pro-rata method in RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, does the bank meet the norm for URCs?

options.text: No; URC outlets are 28.4 of 122.4 (about 23.2%), against the required 25% (30.6)
Yes; URC outlets are 29 of 123 (about 23.6%), which rounds up to the norm
No; URC outlets are 26 of 120 (about 21.7%), as part-time outlets are ignored
Yes; URC outlets are 29 of 120 (about 24.2%), and the norm is 20%

solution.concept: 25% Unbanked Rural Centre norm with part-time outlets
solution.explanation: At least 25% of the Banking Outlets opened in a year must be in URCs. Part-time outlets count pro rata against a 20-hour week (4 hours × 5 days), with at most 4 hours a day counted, in both the numerator (if in a URC) and the denominator. Each part-time outlet = 4 × 4 ÷ 20 = 0.8. Denominator = 120 + 2.4 = 122.4; numerator = 26 + 2.4 = 28.4, about 23.2%, below 25% (which would need 30.6).
solution.why_others_wrong: Part-time outlets count pro rata, not as whole outlets; they are not ignored; the norm is 25%, not 20%.
solution.final_answer: Option A: No; URC outlets are 28.4 of 122.4 (about 23.2%), against the required 25% (30.6)

fact_checks.claim: At least 25 percent of the total number of 'Banking Outlets' opened during a financial year shall be opened in Unbanked Rural Centres (URCs) ... A 'Part-time Banking Outlet', opened in any Centre, will be counted and added to the denominator as well as numerator on pro rata basis
The prescribed period for Banking Outlet is 4 hours per day for 5 days (minimum of 20 hours spread over 5 days) this will remain constant denominator ... a maximum of 4 hours per day will be counted

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework, how are Level 1 assets counted in the stock of high-quality liquid assets (HQLA)?

options.text: Up to 60% of the stock of HQLA, after a 15% haircut
Without any limit and without any haircut, at no more than their current market value
Up to 40% of the stock of HQLA, without a haircut
Without any limit, but after a uniform 50% haircut

solution.explanation: RBI's Asset Liability Management Directions say Level 1 assets can be included in the stock of HQLA without any limit and without applying any haircut, valued at no more than current market value. (From 1 April 2026, Level 1 government securities attract the LAF/MSF haircuts.) Caps of 40% and 15% and haircuts of 15% and 50% apply to Level 2A and Level 2B assets.
steps: Level 2 → 40% cap; Level 2A 15% haircut; Level 2B 50% haircut and 15% cap
solution.why_others_wrong: The 15% and 50% haircuts and the 40% cap belong to Level 2 assets, not Level 1.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Without any limit and without any haircut, at no more than their current market value

fact_checks.claim: Level 1 assets can be included in the stock of HQLA without any limit as also without applying any haircut and shall be valued at an amount not greater than their current market value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Within its mandatory SLR holding, up to what share of its NDTL may a bank count government securities as Level 1 HQLA for the LCR, taking the MSF window and the Facility to Avail Liquidity for LCR (FALLCR) together?

options.text: 16% of NDTL (all under FALLCR)
18% of NDTL (2% under MSF and 16% under FALLCR)
2% of NDTL (only under MSF)
15% of NDTL (3% under MSF and 12% under FALLCR)

solution.explanation: Level 1 assets include government securities within the mandatory SLR to the extent allowed by RBI under MSF, currently 2% of NDTL, and under FALLCR, currently 16% of NDTL, i.e. 18% of NDTL in all, besides securities held in excess of the SLR.
solution.why_others_wrong: 16% and 2% are only one of the two windows; 3%/12% are not RBI's figures.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 18% of NDTL (2% under MSF and 16% under FALLCR)

fact_checks.claim: Within the mandatory SLR requirement, Government securities to the extent allowed by RBI under (a) MSF currently 2 per cent of a bank's Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL), and (b) Facility to Avail Liquidity for Liquidity Coverage Ratio (FALLCR) currently 16 per cent of a bank's NDTL

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A plain-vanilla bond of a non-financial company, rated 'A' by an eligible credit rating agency, trades in a deep and active market and meets RBI's price-stability test. How is it treated in a bank's stock of HQLA for the LCR?

options.text: As a Level 2A asset, with a minimum haircut of 15%
As a Level 1 asset, with no haircut
As a Level 2B asset, with a minimum haircut of 50%
It cannot be included in HQLA at all

solution.concept: Rating bands for corporate bonds in HQLA
solution.explanation: Corporate bonds rated AA- or above (not issued by a bank, FI or NBFC) are Level 2A assets with a 15% haircut. Corporate debt rated between A+ and BBB- that meets the market conditions is a Level 2B asset with a 50% haircut. An 'A' rated bond therefore falls in Level 2B.
solution.why_others_wrong: Level 2A needs AA- or better; corporate bonds are never Level 1; an A-rated non-financial bond meeting the conditions is eligible.
solution.final_answer: Option C: As a Level 2B asset, with a minimum haircut of 50%

fact_checks.claim: Level 2A: Corporate bonds rated AA- or above by an Eligible Credit Rating Agency (ECRA), and not issued by a bank / financial institution / NBFC; minimum 15 per cent haircut
Level 2B: Corporate debt securities, including commercial paper, subject to a 50 per cent haircut ... have a long-term credit rating from an ECRA between A+ and BBB-

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In computing the LCR denominator (total net cash outflows over the next 30 days), up to what limit can a bank count its expected cash inflows?

options.text: Up to 50% of its total expected cash outflows
Up to 100% of its total expected cash outflows
Up to 25% of its stock of HQLA
Up to 75% of its total expected cash outflows

solution.explanation: Total net cash outflows = total expected cash outflows − Min(total expected cash inflows; 75% of total expected cash outflows). The cap ensures that a bank always holds HQLA of at least 25% of its outflows and does not rely only on expected inflows.
solution.why_others_wrong: The cap is 75% of outflows, not 50% or 100%, and it is not linked to HQLA.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Up to 75% of its total expected cash outflows

fact_checks.claim: Total Net Cash Outflows in the next 30 calendar days = total expected cash outflows - Min (total expected cash inflows; 75 per cent of total expected cash outflows)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank holds Level 1 assets of ₹400 crore (already at their HQLA value), Level 2A assets with a market value of ₹200 crore and Level 2B assets with a market value of ₹300 crore, with no short-term repo or reverse repo to unwind. Applying RBI's minimum haircuts and the 15% (Level 2B) and 40% (Level 2) caps, what is its stock of HQLA (approximately)?

options.text: ₹666.7 crore
₹720.0 crore
₹670.0 crore
₹900.0 crore

solution.concept: Stock of HQLA with haircuts and caps
solution.explanation: Adjusted Level 2A = 85% × 200 = 170; adjusted Level 2B = 50% × 300 = 150. Adjustment for the 15% cap = max[150 − 15/85 × (400 + 170), 150 − 15/60 × 400, 0] = max[49.4, 50, 0] = 50. Adjustment for the 40% cap = max[(170 + 150 − 50) − 2/3 × 400, 0] = 270 − 266.7 = 3.3. Stock of HQLA = 400 + 170 + 150 − 50 − 3.3 ≈ ₹666.7 crore. Check: Level 2 is then exactly 40% and Level 2B exactly 15% of the stock.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹720 crore ignores both caps; ₹670 crore applies only the 15% cap; ₹900 crore ignores haircuts and caps.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹666.7 crore

fact_checks.claim: Stock of HQLA = Level 1 + Level 2A + Level 2B - Adjustment for 15 per cent cap - Adjustment for 40 per cent cap; Adjustment for 15 per cent cap = Max [{Adjusted Level 2B - 15/85 * (Adjusted Level 1 + Adjusted Level 2A)}, {Adjusted Level 2B - 15/60 * Adjusted Level 1}, 0]; Adjustment for 40 per cent cap = Max {(Adjusted Level 2A + Adjusted Level 2B - Adjustment for 15 per cent cap) - 2/3 * (Adjusted Level 1 assets), 0}
A minimum 15 per cent haircut shall be applied to the current market value of each Level 2A asset; A minimum haircut of 50 per cent shall be applied to the current market value of each Level 2B asset

questions.question_text:
Consider the following assets of a bank, each meeting RBI's market-liquidity tests:
I. Commercial paper issued by an NBFC, rated equivalent to AA+.
II. Equity shares of a non-financial company included in the Nifty 50 index.
III. A bond of a non-financial company rated BBB-.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Ritu complained to her bank on 1 September 2026. The bank rejected her complaint by a reply dated 12 September 2026, and she is not satisfied. Under RB-IOS, 2026, when can she approach the RBI Ombudsman?

Only after 30 days from her complaint, and by 11 December 2026
Immediately, and by 12 March 2027 (six months from the reply)
Immediately, and no later than 90 days from the bank's reply, i.e. by 11 December 2026

solution.concept: When a complaint can be filed
solution.explanation: The 30-day wait applies only when the regulated entity has not replied. A complainant who has received a reply and is dissatisfied may approach the Ombudsman at once. The complaint must be made within 90 days from the expiry of the reply period or from the RE's last communication, whichever is later; here the last communication is 12 September, so the limit is 12 September + 90 days = 11 December 2026.
steps: Reply received and not satisfied → no need to wait 30 days
solution.why_others_wrong: Waiting 30 days is needed only when there is no reply; six months is not the limit.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Immediately, and no later than 90 days from the bank's reply, i.e. by 11 December 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Customers file complaints against four NBFCs registered with RBI, none of them an excluded type (figures as per the audited balance sheet of the previous year):
P. A deposit-taking NBFC with assets of ₹60 crore.
Q. A non-deposit-taking NBFC with customer interface and assets of ₹150 crore.
R. A deposit-taking NBFC with assets of ₹20 crore.
S. A non-deposit-taking NBFC with customer interface and assets of ₹90 crore.
Against which of them can a complaint be filed under RB-IOS, 2026?

Q only
P, Q, R and S
P, Q and R only

The Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 only

A personal loan sanctioned and disbursed online
An IMPS transfer to another bank
A bill payment from the savings account

Loans, transfers, payments → transactional facility needed

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, what must a bank ensure when it offers mobile banking through USSD or SMS rather than a mobile app?

The service must be restricted to balance enquiry only
The service must be offered only to customers with smartphones

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), RTGS handled 20 crore transactions worth ₹1,246 lakh crore in CY 2021 and 33 crore transactions worth ₹2,206 lakh crore in CY 2025. Which statement is correct?

The average transaction rose from about ₹6.2 lakh to about ₹6.7 lakh

questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), toll plazas onboarded on NETC rose from 964 in December 2021 to 1,896 in December 2025, while FASTags issued grew from 4.42 crore to 11.87 crore. Which statement is correct?

options.text: FASTags grew about 2.7 times and toll plazas about 2 times, so FASTags per plaza rose from about 46,000 to about 63,000
Toll plazas grew faster than FASTags, so FASTags per plaza fell
Both grew about 2.7 times, leaving FASTags per plaza unchanged
FASTags per plaza rose from about 4,600 to about 6,300

solution.explanation: Toll plazas: 1,896 ÷ 964 ≈ 1.97 times. FASTags: 11.87 ÷ 4.42 ≈ 2.69 times. FASTags per plaza: 4.42 crore ÷ 964 ≈ 45,900 in 2021 and 11.87 crore ÷ 1,896 ≈ 62,600 in 2025.
solution.why_others_wrong: FASTags grew faster, so the per-plaza figure rose; the 4,600/6,300 option is off by a factor of ten.
solution.final_answer: Option A: FASTags grew about 2.7 times and toll plazas about 2 times, so FASTags per plaza rose from about 46,000 to about 63,000
